speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me how long you have had the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, and have you noticed if the skin breaks or bleeds easily?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans with early disseminated infection involving the wrist joint). The combination of recent Minnesota camping exposure, a self-resolving monoarticular knee pain (likely a previous "bull's-eye" rash or early Lyme arthritis), and current wrist pain with fever in a 17-year-old male is highly characteristic. I will confirm the diagnosis by reviewing any photos of the skin lesions and requesting a Lyme Serology test.
